title: Native clients keep a refreshed session and can revoke it on sign-out (web half of iOS RF-1012)
acceptance: AUD-007: a session older than Better Auth updateAge gets a Set-Cookie with a later expiry from POST /api/v1/auth/session, the only /api/v1 route that refreshes; every other requireSession route resolves with refresh disabled, so it sets no session cookie and leaves the row due for the next /auth/session; browsers still refresh through Better Auth's get-session; a younger session gets no session Set-Cookie; no 401 carries a Set-Cookie (integration and unit tests).

AUD-009: a native-shaped POST /api/auth/sign-out (cookie, JSON, no Origin/Referer/Sec-Fetch-*) revokes the session, and re-injecting the old cookie gets 401 from POST /api/v1/auth/session (integration test).

Browser CSRF protection is unchanged: sign-out with an untrusted or null Origin, an untrusted Referer, fetch metadata, or a form-shaped body revokes nothing, and other cookie-bearing auth POSTs without Origin are still refused (integration and unit tests).

OpenAPI documents the refresh Set-Cookie header only on POST /auth/session's 200, and api.md, authorization.md and conventions.md describe the /auth/session-only refresh, the no-cookie 401, the client-side current-cookie guard and the sign-out trust boundary; the iOS web-contract snapshots are refreshed in a separate iOS PR.

evidence.summary: iOS code audit AUD-007 (probable 7-day hard expiry) and AUD-009 (probable unrevoked sign-out); both carried by iOS RF-1012.
Owner approved this web change for RF-1012 in the Air session on 2026-11-02.

Before the fix on 8f26519 both findings reproduced: the aged session row was extended but no Set-Cookie reached the client (AUD-007), and native sign-out got 403 MISSING_OR_NULL_ORIGIN with the session still valid (AUD-009). All 13 cases pass after the fix.

Correction 2026-11-02 (third review, owner's narrower redesign): requireSession no longer refreshes or forwards a cookie; only POST /api/v1/auth/session does. Original entry: Forwards refreshed session cookies from /auth/session and requireSession routes, adds withNativeSignOutOrigin for native sign-out, and documents both in OpenAPI and the dev-plan docs. Full local gate green on 0f1438e.

Against a local wrangler dev (port 8799, throwaway vars, MOCK_PROVIDERS): a session aged 2 days got Set-Cookie Max-Age=604800 from POST /api/v1/auth/session; a no-Origin JSON sign-out returned 200 and the old cookie then got 401 from POST /api/v1/auth/session.

Correction 2026-11-02 (third review, owner's narrower redesign): provider connect now keeps its own cookie and gets no session cookie (refresh disabled on ordinary routes); the c.header append fix still applies to /auth/session. Original entry: Final review of #703 at 55adab7 found that forwardSetCookies' c.res assignment let Hono 4.13.14's res setter drop the session cookie on routes that set their own cookie. The new provider-connect case fails with that code (no session cookie) and passes with c.header append. Also added: refresh forwarded exactly once behind many requireSession routers, and the clearing cookie on 401 from /auth/session and /auth/me. 17 integration cases pass.

Correction 2026-11-02 (third review, owner's narrower redesign): the stacked-router unit test now asserts one resolve with disableRefresh, no session cookie forwarded, the route cookie kept and no Set-Cookie on 401. Original entry: Three stacked requireSession routers resolve the session once (getSession called once), forward the refresh once, keep the route's own cookie, and forward the clearing cookie on 401.

Second final review of #703 at 31ff13a: forwarding Better Auth's Max-Age=0 clearing cookie on 401 could let a slow request carrying user A's dead cookie delete user B's cookie after a sign-out and new sign-in (same cookie name). 401s now carry no Set-Cookie (integration and unit tests assert it); the unreachable fallback in forwardSetCookies is removed. The residual race it named (a refresh issued for A arriving after B's sign-in) blocked the third review and led to the redesign below.

Deferred review items, updated after the third review: (1) the native sign-out origin-handling design itself, for the owner; (2) resolved: the once-per-request short-circuit now keys on a sessionResolved flag set only by the session middleware, not userId; (3) c.header copies a finalized Response once per forwarded cookie, now only on POST /auth/session; (4) resolved: the OpenAPI security: [] opt-out is gone with the shared header (the refresh header is only on /auth/session's 200).

Third review of #703 at d0a2428: a refresh Set-Cookie on any 200 could carry account A's token onto B's sign-in. Redesign: only POST /api/v1/auth/session refreshes and forwards the cookie; other routes call getSession with disableRefresh. Integration tests: an aged session on GET /auth/me, GET /explore and provider connect gets no session cookie and an unchanged row; the next /auth/session with the same cookie gets Max-Age=604800 and a later expiry; a fresh session gets none; Better Auth's GET /api/auth/get-session (the SPA's useSession) still refreshes; 401s carry no Set-Cookie. 18 integration and 4 unit cases pass.

resolution: Both audit findings were real and reproduced in integration tests before the fix. After three review rounds, only POST /api/v1/auth/session refreshes the session and returns the refresh cookie; other routes resolve with refresh disabled, no 401 sets a cookie, and native sign-out revokes the session with browser CSRF behaviour pinned by tests. Deferred review items are in the evidence and the PR. The iOS half (persist /auth/session's Set-Cookie only while the request's cookie is still current, treat 401 as signed out, log failed sign-out, reinstall handling) ships in iOS RF-1012/RF-1032 after its web-contract snapshots are refreshed.
